**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 75, verses 1–13:**

Meccan. It has six hundred and fifty-two letters, one hundred and ninety-nine words, and forty verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qayyim al-Faqih informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mu'addil narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Mujahid, from Abd al-Wahid, from al-Hajjaj ibn Abd Allah, from Abu al-Khalil and from Ali ibn Zayd and Ata' ibn Abi Maymuna, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Qiyamah, I and Jibril will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection that he was a believer in the Day of Resurrection, and he will come with his face radiant among the faces of creation on the Day of Resurrection." [65] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/190.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿I do not swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾. The common reading has the alif cut off (maqtu'a) and hamzated: لا أُقْسِمُ.

﴿Nor do I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾. Its form is similar. Al-Hasan and Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj read لأقسم without an alif, connected (mawsula). And ﴿Nor do I swear by the self﴾ with the alif cut off, in the sense that He swore by the Day and did not swear by the self. Similarly, al-Qawwas narrated from Shabl, from Ibn Bukayr. The correct view is that He swore by both of them together.

Regarding the meaning of ﴿I do not swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾, the scholars differed. Some said: the lam is extra (la sila), meaning "I swear by the Day of Resurrection," and this was the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Abu Bakr ibn Abbas said: it is an emphasis of the oath, like your saying "la, wallahi" (no, by Allah). Al-Farra' said regarding the word la: it is a rejection of the words of the polytheists, then He began the oath, saying ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾. He said: every oath that comes after it is a rejection, so la must be placed before it to distinguish between an oath that is a denial and an oath that is a new beginning. Do you not see that you say, beginning, "By Allah, the Messenger is true"? But when you say "La, by Allah, the Messenger is true," it is as if you have emphasized it to a people who denied it.

Aqil informed us that al-Ma'afa informed them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Mis'ar, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqa, from al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, who said: "They do not say al-qiyamah, al-qiyamah; rather, the qiyamah of one of them is his death." And with the same chain, from Sufyan and Mis'ar, from Abu Qays, who said: "I attended a funeral in which Alqama was present. When he was buried, he said: As for this one, his resurrection (qiyamah) has come."

﴿Nor do I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrima said: it blames itself for good and evil, and does not endure patiently in ease and hardship. Mujahid said: it regrets what has passed and blames itself for it, saying "If only I had done it" and "If only I had not done it."

Qatada said: al-lawwama is the corrupt (al-fajira). Ibn Abbas said: it is the blameworthy (al-madhmuma). Al-Farra' said: there is no soul, righteous or corrupt, except that it blames itself. If it has done good, it says, "Why did I not do more?" and if it has done evil, it says, "Would that I had not done it!" Al-Hasan said: it is the soul of the believer. He said: "By Allah, you will not see the believer except that he blames himself: 'What did I intend by my speech? What did I intend by my eating? What did I intend by my inner thought?' As for the corrupt, he goes forward without holding himself to account, and does not rebuke it [[In the manuscript: "and does not rebuke him."]]." Muqatil said: it is the soul of the disbeliever, which blames itself in the Hereafter for what it neglected in the matter of Allah in the world. It was also said: its blame is His saying, ﴿It will say, "Would that I had sent ahead for my life!"﴾ [[Surah al-Fajr: 24.]] and ﴿"Alas for me, for what I neglected concerning Allah's side!"﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 56.]], meaning in the matter of Allah. Sahl said: it is the soul that commands evil, and it is the companion of greed and hope.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: The soul is disbelieving at one time, hypocritical at another, and showing off at another, in all states. It is disbelieving because it does not become accustomed to the truth; it is hypocritical because it does not fulfill covenants; and it is showing off because it does not love to do any deed or take any step except to be seen by people. Whoever has these qualities deserves that blame of it be perpetual.

﴿Does man think﴾.

It was revealed concerning Adi ibn Rabi'a ibn Abi Salama, an ally of Banu Zuhra, the in-law of al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, an ally of Banu Zuhra. The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say: "O Allah, suffice me against the bad neighbor," meaning Adi and al-Akhnas. [66] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/93.]] The reason was that Adi ibn Rabi'a came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said: "O Muhammad, tell me about the Day of Resurrection: when will it happen, and how will its matter and condition be?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) informed him of that. He said:

"If I witnessed that day, I would not believe you and I would not have faith in it. Will Allah gather the bones?"

So Allah, glory be to Him, revealed: ﴿Does man think﴾, meaning the disbeliever.

﴿That We will not gather his bones﴾, after their dispersal and decay, so that We would restore him and resurrect him after death. It is said that He mentioned the bones, but meant his whole self, because the bones are the frame of the creature, and the creature is not complete except by their completeness. It was also said: it is an expression according to the view of the denier, or "Will Allah gather the bones?", like the other saying, ﴿"Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [[Surah Ya-Sin: 78.]].

Then He said, glory be to Him: ﴿Yes, [We are] able﴾, meaning, We are able. The word qadirin (able) is in the future sense, changed to the present. Al-Farra' said: qadirin is in the accusative as a circumstantial state from najma'a (We gather). As if you said in speech: "Does he think that He will not be able to do this to you?" ﴿Yes, able﴾ to [do] greater than that, meaning, "Yes, We are capable, empowered over more than this."

Ibn Abi Ghayla read qadirun with the nominative, meaning "Yes, We are the able." The sense of the verse is: "Yes, We are able to gather his bones and [to do] what is greater than that," namely ﴿to level his fingertips﴾, that is, his fingers. He would make the fingers of his hands and feet one thing, like the sole of a camel, or the hoof of a pig, or the hoof of a donkey, so that he could not do anything with them. But We separated his fingers so that he could grasp with them whatever he wishes, grip when he wishes, and spread out when he wishes, and We made his creation good. This is the view of most of the exegetes.

Al-Qubaysi said: The disbeliever thought that Allah does not resurrect the dead and is not able to gather decayed bones. So Allah, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Yes, [We are] able﴾ to restore the small bones of the fingers despite their smallness, and to join them together until We level the fingertips. Whoever is able to do this is even more able to gather the large bones! This is like a man who said to him: "Do you think you can thread these colocynth [seeds] into a string?" and he replies, "Yes," and [the seeds are] between mustard grains!

﴿Rather, man desires to continue in sin ahead of him﴾. The Exalted says: Does the son of Adam not know that his Lord is able to gather his bones after death? But he wants to continue in sin ahead of him, meaning he goes forward in disobedience to Allah, driving on headlong, not withdrawing from it and not repenting. This is the view of Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ikrima and al-Suddi. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he commits the sin and delays repentance, saying, "I will repent later," until death comes upon him in his worst condition and his most evil deeds. Al-Dahhak said: it is hope; man hopes, saying: "I will live and attain such and such from the world," and does not remember death. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: he denies what lies ahead of him, namely the resurrection and the reckoning. Ibn Kaysan said: he wants that the Hereafter, which is ahead of him, should come to him so that he sees it in the abode of this world.

The root of fujur (sinning) is inclination (al-mayl), and from it the disbeliever and the transgressor are called fajir (corrupt), because of their deviation from the truth. Al-Suddi also said: it means that he wrongs to the extent of his capacity. It was also said: he rides his head in his desire and is concerned wherever his soul leads him.

﴿He asks when is the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning, when is the Day of Resurrection? Then Allah explained that to him, and He, the One who is mighty, said: ﴿So when the sight is dazzled﴾. Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Ibn Abi Ishaq read بَرَقَ (barqa) with an open ra', and others read it with a kasra.

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us, saying: Abu Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, who said: I asked Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' about it, and he said: "Bariqa with a kasra means 'was amazed'." He said: I also asked Abd Allah ibn Abi Ishaq about it, and he said: "Baraqa with a fatha," and he said: "Only the dry colocynth dazzles (baraqa), and the sight dazzles." He said: I mentioned that to Abu Amr, and he said: "The colocynth, the fire and the lightning dazzle; as for the sight, it dazzles at death." He said: I informed Ibn Abi Ishaq of that, and he said: "I took my reading from the shaykhs, Nasr ibn Asim and his companions." I mentioned that to Abu Amr, and he said: "But I do not take from Nasr or his companions." It is as if he meant that he took from the people of the Hijaz.

Qatada and Muqatil said: the sight becomes fixed, so it does not blink at what it sees of the wonders, things it used to deny in the world, that they would not occur. Al-Farra' and al-Khalil said: barqa with a kasra means "was frightened," and the two of them recited for one of the Arabs:

"Be content with your soul and do not seek more, / treat your wounds and do not be frightened."

That is, do not be frightened of the wound you have.

Dhu al-Rumma said:

"Even if Luqman the Wise were to be confronted, / by [the sight of] my beloved unveiled, he would almost be dazzled."

And baraqa with a fatha: he split his eye and opened it. Abu Ubayda recited:

"When Ibn Umayr came to me desiring, / I gave him a yellowish-white camel, so he opened his eye."

That is, he opened his eye. It is also permissible that it be from lightning (al-barq).

﴿And the moon is eclipsed﴾, meaning it became dark and its light went away. Ibn Kaysan said: it may mean "disappeared," like His saying, ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 81.]]. Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa and al-A'raj read khusifa with a damma, because of His saying: ﴿And the sun and the moon are joined﴾ [[Surah al-Qiyamah: 9.]], as black and folded, as if they were two bulls being slaughtered. In the reading of Abd Allah it is: "and the sun and the moon were joined together." It was said: they are joined together in the vanishing of light. Ata' ibn Yasar said: they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection and then thrown into the sea, and they will become the great fire of Allah.

Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Abbas said: they will be placed in the light of the veils.

﴿Man will say on that day, "Where is the escape?"﴾ The refuge (al-mahrab). The common readers read al-mafarr with a fatha on the fa', and Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred it, saying: because it is a verbal noun (masdar). Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan read it with a kasra on the fa'. Al-Kisa'i said: they are two dialects, like madabb and madabb, mashahh and mashihh. Others said: with the fatha it is the verbal noun, and with the kasra it is the place of flight, like al-matla' and al-matli' (the place of rising).

﴿No! No refuge!﴾, meaning, no fortress, no shelter, and no place of safety. Al-Suddi said: "No mountain." When they were frightened they would move toward the mountain and take refuge in it. So Allah, glory be to Him, said: no mountain on that day will protect them.

﴿To your Lord on that day is the final destination﴾.

That is, the destination of creatures, their deeds, and all things. Muqatil said: the end, so he will find no escape from it. Its parallel is ﴿And that to your Lord is the end﴾. Yaman said: the destination and the return. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud. Its parallels are ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾ [[Surah al-Alaq: 8.]], ﴿And to Allah is the destination﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 28.]], and His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned﴾ [[Surah al-Shura: 53.]].

﴿Man will be informed on that day of what he put forward and kept back﴾ [[Surah al-Qiyamah: 13.]]. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas said: "What he put forward" is what he did before his death of good or evil deeds, and "what he kept back" is what he left after his death, a good or bad practice that is followed. Ata' from Ibn Abbas: "What he put forward" refers to disobedience, and "what he kept back" refers to obedience. Mujahid: [it is] the first deed he did and the last. Qatada: "What he put forward" refers to obedience to Allah, and "what he kept back" refers to the right of Allah which he neglected. Ibn Zayd: "What he put forward" refers to deeds, good or evil, and "what he kept back" refers to acting in obedience to Allah without acting on it. Ata: "What he put forward" refers to the beginning of his life, and "what he kept back" refers to the end of his life. Zayd ibn Aslam: "What he put forward" refers to his wealth set aside for himself, and "what he kept back" refers to what he left for the heirs. Its parallel is ﴿A soul will know what it has put forward and kept back﴾ [[Surah al-Infitar: 5.]].

I heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Sa'id ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Uthman say: I heard my father say: I heard Abu Uthman say: "Five calamities in sin are greater than the sin itself:

The first: Allah's abandonment of His servant, until he disobeys Him; had He protected him, he would not have disobeyed.

The second: that He strips him of the adornment of His friends and clothes him in the garments of His enemies.

The third: that He closes the doors of His mercy upon him and opens upon him the doors of His punishment.

The fourth: that He looks at him while he disobeys Him.

The fifth: his standing before Him, while his sins, past and future, are presented to him."

These are the five calamities in sin, which are greater than the sin itself.

I heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Sa'id ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Uthman say: I heard my father say: I heard Abu Uthman say: "Five calamities in sin are greater than the sin itself:

The second: that He strips him of the adornment of His friends and clothes him in the garments of His enemies.

The third: that He closes the doors of His mercy upon him and opens upon him the doors of His punishment.

The fourth: that He looks at him while he disobeys Him.

The fifth: his standing before Him, while his sins, past and future, are presented to him."

These are the five calamities in sin, which are greater than the sin itself.

Whoever has these qualities deserves that blame of it be perpetual.

It was revealed concerning Adi ibn Rabi'a ibn Abi Salama, an ally of Banu Zuhra, the in-law of al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, an ally of Banu Zuhra. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: he denies what lies ahead of him, namely the resurrection and the reckoning. Ibn Kaysan said: he wants that the Hereafter, which is ahead of him, should come to him so that he sees it in the abode of this world.

Al-Suddi also said: it means that he wrongs to the extent of his capacity. It was also said: he rides his head in his desire and is concerned wherever his soul leads him.

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us, saying: Abu Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, who said: I asked Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' about it, and he said: "Bariqa with a kasra means 'was amazed'." He said: I also asked Abd Allah ibn Abi Ishaq about it, and he said: "Baraqa with a fatha," and he said: "Only the dry colocynth dazzles (baraqa), and the sight dazzles." Ata: "What he put forward" refers to the beginning of his life, and "what he kept back" refers to the end of his life. Zayd ibn Aslam: "What he put forward" refers to his wealth set aside for himself, and "what he kept back" refers to what he left for the heirs. ﴿That We will not gather his bones﴾, after their dispersal and decay, so that We would restore him and resurrect him after death. It was also said: it is an expression according to the view of the denier, or "Will Allah gather the bones?", like the other saying, ﴿"Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [[Surah Ya-Sin: 78.]].

Then He said, glory be to Him: ﴿Yes, [We are] able﴾, meaning, We are able. The word qadirin (able) is in the future sense, changed to the present. Al-Farra' said: qadirin is in the accusative as a circumstantial state from najma'a (We gather). As if you said in speech: "Does he think that He will not be able to do this to you?" ﴿Yes, able﴾ to [do] greater than that, meaning, "Yes, We are capable, empowered over more than this."

Ibn Abi Ghayla read qadirun with the nominative, meaning "Yes, We are the able." The sense of the verse is: "Yes, We are able to gather his bones and [to do] what is greater than that," namely ﴿to level his fingertips﴾, that is, his fingers. He would make the fingers of his hands and feet one thing, like the sole of a camel, or the hoof of a pig, or the hoof of a donkey, so that he could not do anything with them. But We separated his fingers so that he could grasp with them whatever he wishes, grip when he wishes, and spread out when he wishes, and We made his creation good. This is the view of most of the exegetes.

Al-Qubaysi said: The disbeliever thought that Allah does not resurrect the dead and is not able to gather decayed bones. So Allah, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Yes, [We are] able﴾ to restore the small bones of the fingers despite their smallness, and to join them together until We level the fingertips. Whoever is able to do this is even more able to gather the large bones! This is like a man who said to him: "Do you think you can thread these colocynth [seeds] into a string?" and he replies, "Yes," and [the seeds are] between mustard grains!

﴿Rather, man desires to continue in sin ahead of him﴾. The Exalted says: Does the son of Adam not know that his Lord is able to gather his bones after death? But he wants to continue in sin ahead of him, meaning he goes forward in disobedience to Allah, driving on headlong, not withdrawing from it and not repenting. This is the view of Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ikrima and al-Suddi. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he commits the sin and delays repentance, saying, "I will repent later," until death comes upon him in his worst condition and his most evil deeds. Al-Dahhak said: it is hope; man hopes, saying: "I will live and attain such and such from the world," and does not remember death. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: he denies what lies ahead of him, namely the resurrection and the reckoning. Ibn Kaysan said: he wants that the Hereafter, which is ahead of him, should come to him so that he sees it in the abode of this world.

The root of fujur (sinning) is inclination (al-mayl), and from it the disbeliever and the transgressor are called fajir (corrupt), because of their deviation from the truth. Al-Suddi also said: it means that he wrongs to the extent of his capacity. It was also said: he rides his head in his desire and is concerned wherever his soul leads him.

﴿He asks when is the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning, when is the Day of Resurrection? Then Allah explained that to him, and He, the One who is mighty, said: ﴿So when the sight is dazzled﴾. Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Ibn Abi Ishaq read بَرَقَ (barqa) with an open ra', and others read it with a kasra.

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us, saying: Abu Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, who said: I asked Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' about it, and he said: "Bariqa with a kasra means 'was amazed'." He said: I also asked Abd Allah ibn Abi Ishaq about it, and he said: "Baraqa with a fatha," and he said: "Only the dry colocynth dazzles (baraqa), and the sight dazzles." He said: I mentioned that to Abu Amr, and he said: "The colocynth, the fire and the lightning dazzle; as for the sight, it dazzles at death." He said: I informed Ibn Abi Ishaq of that, and he said: "I took my reading from the shaykhs, Nasr ibn Asim and his companions." I mentioned that to Abu Amr, and he said: "But I do not take from Nasr or his companions." It is as if he meant that he took from the people of the Hijaz.

Qatada and Muqatil said: the sight becomes fixed, so it does not blink at what it sees of the wonders, things it used to deny in the world, that they would not occur. Al-Farra' and al-Khalil said: barqa with a kasra means "was frightened," and the two of them recited for one of the Arabs:

"Be content with your soul and do not seek more, / treat your wounds and do not be frightened."

That is, do not be frightened of the wound you have.

Dhu al-Rumma said:

"Even if Luqman the Wise were to be confronted, / by [the sight of] my beloved unveiled, he would almost be dazzled."

And baraqa with a fatha: he split his eye and opened it. Abu Ubayda recited:

"When Ibn Umayr came to me desiring, / I gave him a yellowish-white camel, so he opened his eye."

That is, he opened his eye. It is also permissible that it be from lightning (al-barq).

﴿And the moon is eclipsed﴾, meaning it became dark and its light went away. Ibn Kaysan said: it may mean "disappeared," like His saying, ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 81.]]. Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa and al-A'raj read khusifa with a damma, because of His saying: ﴿And the sun and the moon are joined﴾ [[Surah al-Qiyamah: 9.]], as black and folded, as if they were two bulls being slaughtered. In the reading of Abd Allah it is: "and the sun and the moon were joined together." It was said: they are joined together in the vanishing of light. Ata' ibn Yasar said: they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection and then thrown into the sea, and they will become the great fire of Allah.

Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Abbas said: they will be placed in the light of the veils.

﴿Man will say on that day, "Where is the escape?"﴾ The refuge (al-mahrab). The common readers read al-mafarr with a fatha on the fa', and Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred it, saying: because it is a verbal noun (masdar). Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan read it with a kasra on the fa'. Al-Kisa'i said: they are two dialects, like madabb and madabb, mashahh and mashihh. Others said: with the fatha it is the verbal noun, and with the kasra it is the place of flight, like al-matla' and al-matli' (the place of rising).

﴿No! No refuge!﴾, meaning, no fortress, no shelter, and no place of safety. Al-Suddi said: "No mountain." When they were frightened they would move toward the mountain and take refuge in it. So Allah, glory be to Him, said: no mountain on that day will protect them.

﴿To your Lord on that day is the final destination﴾.

That is, the destination of creatures, their deeds, and all things. Muqatil said: the end, so he will find no escape from it. Its parallel is ﴿And that to your Lord is the end﴾. Yaman said: the destination and the return. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud. Its parallels are ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾ [[Surah al-Alaq: 8.]], ﴿And to Allah is the destination﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 28.]], and His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned﴾ [[Surah al-Shura: 53.]].

﴿Man will be informed on that day of what he put forward and kept back﴾ [[Surah al-Qiyamah: 13.]]. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas said: "What he put forward" is what he did before his death of good or evil deeds, and "what he kept back" is what he left after his death, a good or bad practice that is followed. Ata' from Ibn Abbas: "What he put forward" refers to disobedience, and "what he kept back" refers to obedience. Mujahid: [it is] the first deed he did and the last. Qatada: "What he put forward" refers to obedience to Allah, and "what he kept back" refers to the right of Allah which he neglected. Ibn Zayd: "What he put forward" refers to deeds, good or evil, and "what he kept back" refers to acting in obedience to Allah without acting on it. Ata: "What he put forward" refers to the beginning of his life, and "what he kept back" refers to the end of his life. Zayd ibn Aslam: "What he put forward" refers to his wealth set aside for himself, and "what he kept back" refers to what he left for the heirs. Its parallel is ﴿A soul will know what it has put forward and kept back﴾ [[Surah al-Infitar: 5.]].

I heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu Sa'id ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Uthman say: I heard my father say: I heard Abu Uthman say: "Five calamities in sin are greater than the sin itself:

The first: Allah's abandonment of His servant, until he disobeys Him; had He protected him, he would not have disobeyed.

The second: that He strips him of the adornment of His friends and clothes him in the garments of His enemies.

The third: that He closes the doors of His mercy upon him and opens upon him the doors of His punishment.

The fourth: that He looks at him while he disobeys Him.

The fifth: his standing before Him, while his sins, past and future, are presented to him."

These are the five calamities in sin, which are greater than the sin itself.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 75, verse 14–28:

﴿Nay, man is a witness against himself.﴾

Ikrimah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: its meaning is, "Nay, man is a witness against himself from within himself, watchers who observe his deeds and testify against him with them, and they are: his hearing, his sight, his hands, his feet and all his limbs." This is the narration of Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Qubbi said: he placed his limbs in the position of his self, and therefore the verb is feminine (raat). It is also permissible that the feminine form (baṣīrah) is due to its being attached to "self (nafs)," as you say in speech: "some of his fingers went (dhahabat ba'ḍu aṣābi'ihi)." And baṣīrah is nominative as the predicate of the preposition-phrase, which is his saying ﴿ʿalā nafsihi﴾ ("against himself"). It may also mean "Nay, man against himself is with insight (bi-baṣīrah)," and the preposition was then dropped, as in His saying: ﴿wa-in aradtum an tastarḍiʿū awlādakum﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:233], meaning "for your children." It may also be an adjective for a feminine noun, meaning "Nay, for man against himself there is an insightful eye (ʿayn baṣīrah)." Al-Farra' recited:

"As if upon the one of intellect there is an insightful eye,
regarding his seat or the sight that he sees.
He is wary, until he thinks all people
from fear, and his inner secrets are not hidden from him."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/100.]

Abu al-Aliyah and Ata' said: "Nay, man against himself is a witness," and this is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. The ta' in baṣīrah is for emphasis (lil-mubalaghah). Al-Akhfash said: it is like your saying "fulan ʿibrah" and "ḥujjah" (a man who is a lesson, a proof). The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of God Most High: ﴿Sufficient is your own self against you today as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra' 17:14]. Ibn Taghlib said: al-baṣīrah, al-bayyinah, al-shahid and al-dalil are one and the same.

﴿Even if he presents his excuses﴾: meaning, a witness will testify against him even if he makes excuses and argues on behalf of himself.

Its like is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿On a day when no excuse will benefit the wrongdoers﴾ [Ghafir 40:52] and His saying: ﴿nor will they be permitted, so that they may make excuses﴾ [Al-Mursalat 77:36]. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Zayd, Abu al-Aliyah and Ata'. Al-Farra' said: even if he makes an excuse, there is within himself one who will refute his excuse. Muqatil said: even if he puts forward an excuse or an argument, that will not benefit him.

The meaning of "ilqa'" (presenting) is "speech," like His saying: ﴿So they will say to them, "You are indeed liars"﴾ [Al-Nahl 16:86] and ﴿and they will offer peace to God on that day﴾ [Al-Nahl 16:87]. Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it means even if he lets down curtains and closes doors. He said: the people of Yemen call a curtain "al-mi'dhar." Some of the scholars of meanings said: "al-ma'adhir" is one of them shifting the blame onto another.

﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it﴾

This is because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) would not cease reciting the Qur'an, fearing that he would forget it. When Jibril would descend to him with the Qur'an, Jibril would not finish the verse until the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) had recited its beginning, and he would move his tongue with it within himself, fearing that he would forget it. So God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:114], and He revealed: ﴿We shall make you recite, and you will not forget﴾ [Al-A'la 87:6], and He revealed: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it﴾, meaning with the revelation, ﴿your tongue﴾, ﴿with it﴾, meaning its recitation, so that you may memorize it and not forget it. ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection﴾, in your heart until you memorize it, ﴿and its recitation﴾ and its reading to you until you comprehend it. It was said that by His saying ﴿wa-qur'anahu﴾ ("and its recitation") He meant its collection in your heart, and it is a verbal noun like "al-rujhan" and "al-nuqsan" (outweighing and diminishing).

﴿So when We have recited it﴾ to you, ﴿follow its recitation﴾, meaning what it contains of rulings. ﴿Then upon Us is its explanation﴾, with what it contains of the limits, the lawful and the unlawful. ﴿No! Rather, you love the immediate [life]and leave the Hereafter﴾. Ahl al-Madinah and al-Kufah read both with the ta' (second person), and others with the ya' (third person), meaning they choose this world over the reward. Its parallel is in Surat al-Insan: ﴿Indeed, these love the immediate [life] and leave behind them a heavy day﴾ [Al-Insan 76:27].

﴿Faces that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿will be radiant﴾. Ibn Abbas said: beautiful. Al-Hasan said: God beautified them by looking at their Lord. Mujahid: joyful. Ibn Zayd: blessed. Muqatil: white, with light over them. Al-Suddi: shining. Yaman: bright. Al-Farra': illuminated with bliss. Al-Kisa'i: delight. Al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: it is said "nadhdhara Allahu wajha fulan," so he is radiant, and his face becomes "nadir" and "nadrah" and "nadarah." God, glorified is He, said: ﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 83:24].

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «May God make radiant the man who heard my saying and preserved it» [Musnad Ahmad: 4/80]. And he considered in this verse His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing﴾ [Abasa 80:38–39].

﴿Looking at their Lord﴾. Most people say: they will look at their Lord with direct vision.

Al-Husayn ibn Waqid said: Yazid ibn Ikrimah, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid and some elders of the people of Kufah informed me, saying: "They will look at their Lord, looking." Al-Hasan said: they will look at the Creator, and it is right that they be radiant while they look at the Creator. Ata' al-Awfi said: they look at God; their sight does not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them. This is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision﴾ [Al-An'am 6:103]. The evidence for this interpretation is what:

Al-Hasan ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Majah related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Mandah al-Isbahani related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Hafs related to us, saying: Isra'il ibn Yunus related to us from Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Indeed, the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks at his gardens, his wives, his bounties, his servants and his couches for a distance of a thousand years, and indeed the most honoured of them before God is the one who looks at His Face, blessed and exalted, morning and evening.» Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) recited: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord﴾ [Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/93].

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu al-Nafkh Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi al-Mawsili related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Isa ibn al-Sakin related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yunus al-Yamami related to us, saying: Rabah ibn Zayd al-San'ani informed us, saying: Ibn Juraij informed me, saying: Ziyad ibn Sa'd informed me that Abu al-Zubayr informed him from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will manifest Himself until they look at His Face, and they will fall down prostrating to Him. Then He will say: "Raise your heads, for this is not a day of worship."» [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/109.]

And al-Hasan narrated from Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: among the supplications of the Prophet (peace be upon him) was: «O God, I ask You for the delight of looking at Your Face and longing for meeting You, without harmful distress or misleading trial.» [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 1/388.] He means that they await the reward from their Lord, and they do not see anything behind Him.

I say: this interpretation is flawed, because when the Arabs intend by "nazar" (looking) the sense of "waiting," they say "nazartuhu," as God, glorified is He, said: ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour?﴾ [Muhammad 47:18]; ﴿Do they await anything but the fire of God?﴾; and ﴿They await only a single Cry﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:49]. And when they intend by it reflection and deliberation, they say "nazartu fihi." But when "nazar" is joined with "ila" and with the mention of "wajh" (face), it can only mean seeing and direct vision.

﴿And faces that Day will be gloomy﴾: frowning, dark, altered, blackened. ﴿They will think that a calamity will be done to them﴾. Mujahid said: a disaster. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: a back-breaking calamity; its origin is "al-fiqrah" and "al-fiqar" (vertebrae), and it is said "faqarahu" when one breaks his vertebra, as it is said "ra'asahu" when one strikes his head. Qatadah said: al-fathirah is evil. Ibn Zayd said: they know that they will enter the Fire. Abu Ubaydah said: al-fathirah is the calamity; it is said "ʿamila bihā al-fāqirah," and its origin is branding on the nose of a camel with iron or fire until it reaches the bone. Al-Kalbi said: a terrible punishment, and it is the veil.

﴿No! When it reaches the collarbones﴾, meaning the soul, a metonymy for something unmentioned, ﴿al-taraqi﴾, so that it rattles at death. The taraqi are the bones flanking the hollow of the throat on the right and left. Duraid ibn al-Simmah said:

"And many a great one I defended them with,
when their souls had reached the collarbones."
[Balaghat al-Nisa': 197; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/111.]

﴿And it is said﴾, and those present say: ﴿"Who is a healer?"﴾, is there any physician who will treat him and cure him? Qatadah said: they sought physicians for him, but they did not avail him anything of the decree.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: al-Sunni Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Habbab al-Jumahi related to us, saying: Musaddad ibn Musarhad related to us from Khalid ibn Abd Allah from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he cauterized a slave of his. I said: "Do you cauterize?" He said: "Yes, make the Arabs Jews."

Ibn Mas'ud informed us that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: «Indeed God, glorified is He, has not sent down any disease without sending down with it a cure, which he who is ignorant of it does not know, and he who knows it knows.» [Musnad Ahmad: 1/446.] Sulayman al-Taymi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: this is the saying of the angels, one of them saying to another: "Who will ascend with his soul?" Angels of mercy and angels of punishment ascend with it. This is the narration of Abu al-Jawza' from Ibn Abbas. Abu al-Aliyah said: the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment dispute over it, which of them will ascend with his soul.

﴿And he thinks that it is separation﴾: a separation unlike any other separation, in which hope of reunion has been cut off.

Al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Khatami and Muhammad ibn Aqil al-Khuza'i informed us, both saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Uqbah al-Shaybani informed us, saying: al-Khidr ibn Aban al-Qurashi informed us, saying: Ibn Maytham ibn Hadiyyah related to us from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: «Indeed the servant struggles with the agony of death and its convulsions, and indeed his joints greet one another, saying: "Peace be upon you, you are parting from me and I part from you until the Day of Resurrection."» [Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/563, no. 42183.]

from fear, and his inner secrets are not hidden from him."
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/100.]

from fear, and his inner secrets are not hidden from him."

Muqatil said: even if he puts forward an excuse or an argument, that will not benefit him.

Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it means even if he lets down curtains and closes doors. He said: the people of Yemen call a curtain "al-mi'dhar." Some of the scholars of meanings said: "al-ma'adhir" is one of them shifting the blame onto another.

This is because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) would not cease reciting the Qur'an, fearing that he would forget it. It was said that by His saying ﴿wa-qur'anahu﴾ ("and its recitation") He meant its collection in your heart, and it is a verbal noun like "al-rujhan" and "al-nuqsan" (outweighing and diminishing).

Its parallel is in Surat al-Insan: ﴿Indeed, these love the immediate [life] and leave behind them a heavy day﴾ [Al-Insan 76:27].

﴿Faces that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿will be radiant﴾. Ibn Abbas said: beautiful. Al-Hasan said: God beautified them by looking at their Lord. Mujahid: joyful. Ibn Zayd: blessed. Muqatil: white, with light over them. Al-Suddi: shining. Yaman: bright. Al-Farra': illuminated with bliss. Al-Kisa'i: delight. Al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: it is said "nadhdhara Allahu wajha fulan," so he is radiant, and his face becomes "nadir" and "nadrah" and "nadarah." God, glorified is He, said: ﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 83:24].

Al-Hasan said: they will look at the Creator, and it is right that they be radiant while they look at the Creator. Ata' al-Awfi said: they look at God; their sight does not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them. This is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision﴾ [Al-An'am 6:103]. The evidence for this interpretation is what:

Al-Hasan ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Majah related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Mandah al-Isbahani related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Hafs related to us, saying: Isra'il ibn Yunus related to us from Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Indeed, the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks at his gardens, his wives, his bounties, his servants and his couches for a distance of a thousand years, and indeed the most honoured of them before God is the one who looks at His Face, blessed and exalted, morning and evening.» Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) recited: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord﴾ [Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/93].

Abu Ubaydah said: al-fathirah is the calamity; it is said "ʿamila bihā al-fāqirah," and its origin is branding on the nose of a camel with iron or fire until it reaches the bone. Al-Kalbi said: a terrible punishment, and it is the veil.

"And many a great one I defended them with,
when their souls had reached the collarbones."
[Balaghat al-Nisa': 197; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/111.]

Al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: it is said "nadhdhara Allahu wajha fulan," so he is radiant, and his face becomes "nadir" and "nadrah" and "nadarah." Abu Ubaydah said: al-fathirah is the calamity; it is said "ʿamila bihā al-fāqirah," and its origin is branding on the nose of a camel with iron or fire until it reaches the bone. Al-Kalbi said: a terrible punishment, and it is the veil.

"And many a great one I defended them with,
when their souls had reached the collarbones."
[Balaghat al-Nisa': 197; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/111.]

[Balaghat al-Nisa': 197; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/111.]

Muqatil: white, with light over them. Al-Suddi: shining. Yaman: bright. Al-Farra': illuminated with bliss. Al-Kisa'i: delight. Al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: it is said "nadhdhara Allahu wajha fulan," so he is radiant, and his face becomes "nadir" and "nadrah" and "nadarah." God, glorified is He, said: ﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 83:24].

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «May God make radiant the man who heard my saying and preserved it» [Musnad Ahmad: 4/80]. And he considered in this verse His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing﴾ [Abasa 80:38–39].

﴿Looking at their Lord﴾. Most people say: they will look at their Lord with direct vision.

Al-Husayn ibn Waqid said: Yazid ibn Ikrimah, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid and some elders of the people of Kufah informed me, saying: "They will look at their Lord, looking." Al-Hasan said: they will look at the Creator, and it is right that they be radiant while they look at the Creator. Ata' al-Awfi said: they look at God; their sight does not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them. This is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision﴾ [Al-An'am 6:103]. The evidence for this interpretation is what:

Al-Hasan ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Majah related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Mandah al-Isbahani related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Hafs related to us, saying: Isra'il ibn Yunus related to us from Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Indeed, the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks at his gardens, his wives, his bounties, his servants and his couches for a distance of a thousand years, and indeed the most honoured of them before God is the one who looks at His Face, blessed and exalted, morning and evening.» Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) recited: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord﴾ [Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/93].

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu al-Nafkh Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi al-Mawsili related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Isa ibn al-Sakin related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yunus al-Yamami related to us, saying: Rabah ibn Zayd al-San'ani informed us, saying: Ibn Juraij informed me, saying: Ziyad ibn Sa'd informed me that Abu al-Zubayr informed him from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: «Our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will manifest Himself until they look at His Face, and they will fall down prostrating to Him. Then He will say: "Raise your heads, for this is not a day of worship."» [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/109.]

And al-Hasan narrated from Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: among the supplications of the Prophet (peace be upon him) was: «O God, I ask You for the delight of looking at Your Face and longing for meeting You, without harmful distress or misleading trial.» [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 1/388.] He means that they await the reward from their Lord, and they do not see anything behind Him.

I say: this interpretation is flawed, because when the Arabs intend by "nazar" (looking) the sense of "waiting," they say "nazartuhu," as God, glorified is He, said: ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour?﴾ [Muhammad 47:18]; ﴿Do they await anything but the fire of God?﴾; and ﴿They await only a single Cry﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:49]. And when they intend by it reflection and deliberation, they say "nazartu fihi." But when "nazar" is joined with "ila" and with the mention of "wajh" (face), it can only mean seeing and direct vision.

﴿And faces that Day will be gloomy﴾: frowning, dark, altered, blackened. ﴿They will think that a calamity will be done to them﴾. Mujahid said: a disaster. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: a back-breaking calamity; its origin is "al-fiqrah" and "al-fiqar" (vertebrae), and it is said "faqarahu" when one breaks his vertebra, as it is said "ra'asahu" when one strikes his head. Qatadah said: al-fathirah is evil. Ibn Zayd said: they know that they will enter the Fire. Abu Ubaydah said: al-fathirah is the calamity; it is said "ʿamila bihā al-fāqirah," and its origin is branding on the nose of a camel with iron or fire until it reaches the bone. Al-Kalbi said: a terrible punishment, and it is the veil.

﴿No! When it reaches the collarbones﴾, meaning the soul, a metonymy for something unmentioned, ﴿al-taraqi﴾, so that it rattles at death. The taraqi are the bones flanking the hollow of the throat on the right and left. Duraid ibn al-Simmah said:

"And many a great one I defended them with,
when their souls had reached the collarbones."
[Balaghat al-Nisa': 197; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/111.]

﴿And it is said﴾, and those present say: ﴿"Who is a healer?"﴾, is there any physician who will treat him and cure him? Qatadah said: they sought physicians for him, but they did not avail him anything of the decree.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: al-Sunni Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Habbab al-Jumahi related to us, saying: Musaddad ibn Musarhad related to us from Khalid ibn Abd Allah from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he cauterized a slave of his. I said: "Do you cauterize?" He said: "Yes, make the Arabs Jews."

Ibn Mas'ud informed us that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: «Indeed God, glorified is He, has not sent down any disease without sending down with it a cure, which he who is ignorant of it does not know, and he who knows it knows.» [Musnad Ahmad: 1/446.] Sulayman al-Taymi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: this is the saying of the angels, one of them saying to another: "Who will ascend with his soul?" Angels of mercy and angels of punishment ascend with it. This is the narration of Abu al-Jawza' from Ibn Abbas. Abu al-Aliyah said: the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment dispute over it, which of them will ascend with his soul.

﴿And he thinks that it is separation﴾: a separation unlike any other separation, in which hope of reunion has been cut off.

Al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Khatami and Muhammad ibn Aqil al-Khuza'i informed us, both saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Uqbah al-Shaybani informed us, saying: al-Khidr ibn Aban al-Qurashi informed us, saying: Ibn Maytham ibn Hadiyyah related to us from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: «Indeed the servant struggles with the agony of death and its convulsions, and indeed his joints greet one another, saying: "Peace be upon you, you are parting from me and I part from you until the Day of Resurrection."» [Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/563, no. 42183.]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 75, verses 29–40:**

وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ "And the shin is wound around the shin" (﴿And one leg is entwined with another﴾). Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "The world is joined to the Hereafter." This is also the report of Abu al-Jawza' and 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas, and the report of 'Awf and Mansur from al-Hasan. Al-Wali and Badhan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The affair of this world is joined to the affair of the Hereafter, so it is the last day of the days of this world and the first day of the days of the Hereafter." This is the report of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid. Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid said: "The deeds of this world are joined to the deeds of the Hereafter." Al-Dahhak said: "The people prepare his body and the angels prepare his soul." Sufyan narrated from a man, from al-Hasan, from Mujahid, the two of them saying: "Life and death are gathered in him." Qatadah said: "Hardship upon hardship." Bishr ibn al-Muhajir reported from al-Hasan who said: "They are your two shins when they are wrapped in the shroud," and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab held this view.

We were informed by 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid, who said: Abu Muhammad al-Muzani informed us, who said: Mutayyin related to us, who said: Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, who said: Khalid ibn Qays related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: "His legs died and did not carry him, and they were upon him as a burden." Shu'bah reported from Qatadah who said: "An affair that comes to him when one leg strikes the other." Abu Malik: "He puts them on at death." 'Ikrimah: "Departure from the world to the Hereafter." Abu Yahya from Mujahid: "Affliction upon affliction."

Al-Qurtubi: "The affair upon the affair." Zayd ibn Aslam: "The shroud's shin joined to the corpse's shin." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Calamities followed one upon another upon him." Al-Suddi: "He does not emerge from one distress except that a greater one comes to him." The Arabs mention the shin only in trials and hardships, and from their well-known proverb: "He does not loose the shin except while holding a shin." Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

"I have been kept awake by a worry that visits me, and the soul is full of scruples and anxieties,
Seeking refuge in the gravel when the night of completeness kept me awake, which I endure on a shin."

That is: upon weariness and hardship.

Ibn 'Ata' said: "There gathers upon him the hardship of departing the homeland of the world, family and children, and the hardship of coming before his Lord, not knowing what he will be presented with." For this reason 'Uthman ibn 'Affan said: "I have never seen a scene except that the grave is more frightful than it, because it is the last of the abodes of this world and the first of the abodes of the Hereafter." Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "When the deceased enters the grave, four angels stand at the edge of his grave: one at his head, a second at his feet, a third on his right, and a fourth on his left. The one at his head says: 'O son of Adam, the terms have ended and the hopes have been cut off.' The one on his right says: 'Wealth has gone and deeds remain.' The one on his left says: 'Preoccupations have gone and calamity remains.' The one at his feet says: 'Blessed are you for your earnings, if your earnings were lawful and you were occupied in serving the Lord of Majesty.'"

إِلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَساقُ ﴿To your Lord, that Day, is the driving﴾: the final end and the return. The angels drive his soul to where Allah, the Exalted, has commanded them.

فَلا صَدَّقَ ﴿So he neither believed﴾, meaning Abu Jahl. وَلا صَلَّى ﴿nor prayed﴾. وَلكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى ﴿But he denied and turned away﴾. ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى ﴿Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾: strutting with pride. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "It is the gait of the Banu Makhzum." Its root is from al-mata', meaning the back, i.e., he twists his back out of arrogance. It was also said that its root is yatamatta', meaning he stretches, and al-mat is stretching; one of the two ta's was changed to ya'. This matter has already passed. And "tamata al-insan" means that a person stood up from his sleep and stretched out.

Al-Husayn informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Hamadhani related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Makhlad al-Farqadi related to us, who said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Shadhakuni related to us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Utbah related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, who heard an old shaykh called Bajnas, client of al-Zubayr, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When my community walks the *mutayTaa'* (the arrogant gait) and the Romans and Persians serve them, Allah will set some of them against others." [73] Sufyan said: I was informed of this hadith by Ibn Abi Najih, who said: "Do you know what al-mutayTaa' is? It is like His statement, the Exalted: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى ﴿then he went to his family, swaggering﴾."

أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى ثُمَّ أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى ﴿Woe to you, and woe; then again, woe to you, and woe﴾. This is a threat from Allah, the Exalted, upon the threat of Abu Jahl. It is a word established for warning and menace. Al-Khansa' said:

"I resolved to put myself through all cares, so woe to my self, woe to it."

Abu al-Qayyim al-Sadusi recited to me, who said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi al-Adabi recited to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Taghlib recited to us:

"O Aws, if our spears were to reach you, you would be like one whom the Abyss throws down.
Your eyes have been fixed at the back of the neck, woe to you, and woe, for this one who guards you."

Some scholars said: its meaning is that you are more deserving of this punishment and more entitled to it; "awla" (more fitting). It is said of a man who suffers a hardship that he deserves. It was also said: it is a phrase the Arabs say to one whom harm is approaching, and its origin is from *wali*, meaning nearness. Allah, the Exalted, said: قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُمْ ﴿Fight those who are near you﴾ [Q. 9:123]. It is said: "Then the one who follows him," i.e., who is near him. The poet said:

"They charged a charge against those near them, and we charged a charge against those near us."

Another said:

"Ghadub has forsaken me, and the love of one who keeps away; and the enemy has turned away from your protector, scattered."

Abu al-Qayyim al-Halabi, the teacher, related to us that he heard Abu al-Haytham al-Jummi, who was knowledgeable in meanings, say, relating from some scholars: that His saying أَوْلى is an inverted form, its meaning being: *awyal* from *al-waylu* (woe), just as one says *ma atyabahu* and *ayyabahu*, *'aqani* and *'aqani*, *ayyim* and *ayyami*; its origin is *ayayim*, and *qaws* and *qusiyy*, whose origin is *qu'uws*. The meaning of the verse is as if He were saying to Abu Jahl: "Woe to you on the day you die, woe to you on the day you are raised, woe to you on the day you enter the Fire and abide in it forever."

Qatadah said: "It was mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) seized the collar of Abu Jahl's garment in al-Batha' and said to him: أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى ثُمَّ أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى." Abu Jahl said: "Do you threaten me, O Muhammad? By Allah, neither you nor your Lord can do anything to me, and I am mightier than whoever walks between its two mountains." Then, on the day of Badr, he looked down upon them and said: "We shall not worship Allah after today." [74] Allah struck him with the worst of deaths and killed him in the most wretched manner; the two sons of 'Afra' finished him off, and Ibn Mas'ud dispatched him. Qatadah said: "It was also mentioned to us that Abu Jahl used to say: 'If I knew that Muhammad was the Messenger of Allah, I would not follow a youth of Quraysh.'" He said: "It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say: 'Every nation has a Pharaoh, and the Pharaoh of this nation is Abu Jahl.'" [75]

أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ أَنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدىً ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected?﴾ Meaning: idle, unordered and unforbidden. It is said: "asdaytu hajati," meaning I wasted my need; and "abil sudan" means a camel grazing wherever it wishes without a herdsman. أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنى ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ al-Hasan, Ibn Muhaysin, Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Salam recited it with the *ya'* (yumna), and this is the transmission of al-Mufaddal and Hafs from 'Asim, and the preference of Abu 'Ubayd because of *al-mani*; the rest recited it with the *ta'* (tumna) because of *al-nutfah*, and this is the preference of Abu Hatim.

ثُمَّ كانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى ﴿Then he became a clinging clot, then He created and proportioned﴾: proportioned his creation. فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى ﴿And made of him two sexes, the male and the female.﴾ أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ الذي فعل هذا بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى ﴿Is not He who did this able to give life to the dead?﴾

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: al-Qati'i related to us, who said: al-Kindi related to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Bannan al-Saffar related to us, who said: Shu'bah related to us, who said: Yunus al-Tawil, companion of Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, related to me, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: When this verse was revealed, أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Glory be to You, and yes." [76]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Rabi'i related to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ayyub al-Makhzumi related to us, who said: Salih ibn Malik related to us, who said: Abu Nawfal 'Ali ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever recites سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلى, whether he is an imam or otherwise, let him say: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.' And whoever recites لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ, and when he reaches its end, let him say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and yes,' whether he is an imam or otherwise."

وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ "And the shin is wound around the shin" (﴿And one leg is entwined with another﴾). Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "The world is joined to the Hereafter." This is also the report of Abu al-Jawza' and 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas, and the report of 'Awf and Mansur from al-Hasan. Al-Wali and Badhan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The affair of this world is joined to the affair of the Hereafter, so it is the last day of the days of this world and the first day of the days of the Hereafter." This is the report of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid. Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid said: "The deeds of this world are joined to the deeds of the Hereafter." Al-Dahhak said: "The people prepare his body and the angels prepare his soul." Sufyan narrated from a man, from al-Hasan, from Mujahid, the two of them saying: "Life and death are gathered in him." Qatadah said: "Hardship upon hardship." Bishr ibn al-Muhajir reported from al-Hasan who said: "They are your two shins when they are wrapped in the shroud," and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab held this view.

We were informed by 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid, who said: Abu Muhammad al-Muzani informed us, who said: Mutayyin related to us, who said: Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, who said: Khalid ibn Qays related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: "His legs died and did not carry him, and they were upon him as a burden." Shu'bah reported from Qatadah who said: "An affair that comes to him when one leg strikes the other." Abu Malik: "He puts them on at death." 'Ikrimah: "Departure from the world to the Hereafter." Abu Yahya from Mujahid: "Affliction upon affliction."

Al-Qurtubi: "The affair upon the affair." Zayd ibn Aslam: "The shroud's shin joined to the corpse's shin." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Calamities followed one upon another upon him." Al-Suddi: "He does not emerge from one distress except that a greater one comes to him." The Arabs mention the shin only in trials and hardships, and from their well-known proverb: "He does not loose the shin except while holding a shin." Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

"I have been kept awake by a worry that visits me, and the soul is full of scruples and anxieties,
Seeking refuge in the gravel when the night of completeness kept me awake, which I endure on a shin."

That is: upon weariness and hardship.

Ibn 'Ata' said: "There gathers upon him the hardship of departing the homeland of the world, family and children, and the hardship of coming before his Lord, not knowing what he will be presented with." For this reason 'Uthman ibn 'Affan said: "I have never seen a scene except that the grave is more frightful than it, because it is the last of the abodes of this world and the first of the abodes of the Hereafter." Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "When the deceased enters the grave, four angels stand at the edge of his grave: one at his head, a second at his feet, a third on his right, and a fourth on his left. The one at his head says: 'O son of Adam, the terms have ended and the hopes have been cut off.' The one on his right says: 'Wealth has gone and deeds remain.' The one on his left says: 'Preoccupations have gone and calamity remains.' The one at his feet says: 'Blessed are you for your earnings, if your earnings were lawful and you were occupied in serving the Lord of Majesty.'"

إِلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَساقُ ﴿To your Lord, that Day, is the driving﴾: the final end and the return. The angels drive his soul to where Allah, the Exalted, has commanded them.

فَلا صَدَّقَ ﴿So he neither believed﴾, meaning Abu Jahl. وَلا صَلَّى ﴿nor prayed﴾. وَلكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى ﴿But he denied and turned away﴾. ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى ﴿Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾: strutting with pride. Zayd ibn Aslam said: "It is the gait of the Banu Makhzum." Its root is from al-mata', meaning the back, i.e., he twists his back out of arrogance. It was also said that its root is yatamatta', meaning he stretches, and al-mat is stretching; one of the two ta's was changed to ya'. This matter has already passed. And "tamata al-insan" means that a person stood up from his sleep and stretched out.

Al-Husayn informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Hamadhani related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Makhlad al-Farqadi related to us, who said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Shadhakuni related to us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Utbah related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, who heard an old shaykh called Bajnas, client of al-Zubayr, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When my community walks the *mutayTaa'* (the arrogant gait) and the Romans and Persians serve them, Allah will set some of them against others." [73] Sufyan said: I was informed of this hadith by Ibn Abi Najih, who said: "Do you know what al-mutayTaa' is? It is like His statement, the Exalted: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى ﴿then he went to his family, swaggering﴾."

أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى ثُمَّ أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى ﴿Woe to you, and woe; then again, woe to you, and woe﴾. This is a threat from Allah, the Exalted, upon the threat of Abu Jahl. It is a word established for warning and menace. Al-Khansa' said:

"I resolved to put myself through all cares, so woe to my self, woe to it."

Abu al-Qayyim al-Sadusi recited to me, who said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi al-Adabi recited to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Taghlib recited to us:

"O Aws, if our spears were to reach you, you would be like one whom the Abyss throws down.
Your eyes have been fixed at the back of the neck, woe to you, and woe, for this one who guards you."

Some scholars said: its meaning is that you are more deserving of this punishment and more entitled to it; "awla" (more fitting). It is said of a man who suffers a hardship that he deserves. It was also said: it is a phrase the Arabs say to one whom harm is approaching, and its origin is from *wali*, meaning nearness. Another said:

Abu al-Qayyim al-Halabi, the teacher, related to us that he heard Abu al-Haytham al-Jummi, who was knowledgeable in meanings, say, relating from some scholars: that His saying أَوْلى is an inverted form, its meaning being: *awyal* from *al-waylu* (woe), just as one says *ma atyabahu* and *ayyabahu*, *'aqani* and *'aqani*, *ayyim* and *ayyami*; its origin is *ayayim*, and *qaws* and *qusiyy*, whose origin is *qu'uws*. Al-Husayn informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Hamadhani related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Makhlad al-Farqadi related to us, who said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Shadhakuni related to us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Utbah related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, who heard an old shaykh called Bajnas, client of al-Zubayr, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When my community walks the *mutayTaa'* (the arrogant gait) and the Romans and Persians serve them, Allah will set some of them against others." [73] Sufyan said: I was informed of this hadith by Ibn Abi Najih, who said: "Do you know what al-mutayTaa' is? It is like His statement, the Exalted: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى ﴿then he went to his family, swaggering﴾."

أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى ثُمَّ أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى ﴿Woe to you, and woe; then again, woe to you, and woe﴾. This is a threat from Allah, the Exalted, upon the threat of Abu Jahl. It is a word established for warning and menace. Al-Khansa' said:

"I resolved to put myself through all cares, so woe to my self, woe to it."

Abu al-Qayyim al-Sadusi recited to me, who said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi al-Adabi recited to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Taghlib recited to us:

"O Aws, if our spears were to reach you, you would be like one whom the Abyss throws down.
Your eyes have been fixed at the back of the neck, woe to you, and woe, for this one who guards you."

Some scholars said: its meaning is that you are more deserving of this punishment and more entitled to it; "awla" (more fitting). It is said of a man who suffers a hardship that he deserves. It was also said: it is a phrase the Arabs say to one whom harm is approaching, and its origin is from *wali*, meaning nearness. "They charged a charge against those near them, and we charged a charge against those near us."

Another said:

"Ghadub has forsaken me, and the love of one who keeps away; and the enemy has turned away from your protector, scattered."

Abu al-Qayyim al-Halabi, the teacher, related to us that he heard Abu al-Haytham al-Jummi, who was knowledgeable in meanings, say, relating from some scholars: that His saying أَوْلى is an inverted form, its meaning being: *awyal* from *al-waylu* (woe), just as one says *ma atyabahu* and *ayyabahu*, *'aqani* and *'aqani*, *ayyim* and *ayyami*; its origin is *ayayim*, and *qaws* and *qusiyy*, whose origin is *qu'uws*. He said: "It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say: 'Every nation has a Pharaoh, and the Pharaoh of this nation is Abu Jahl.'" [75]

أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ أَنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدىً ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected?﴾ Meaning: idle, unordered and unforbidden. ثُمَّ كانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى ﴿Then he became a clinging clot, then He created and proportioned﴾: proportioned his creation. فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى ﴿And made of him two sexes, the male and the female.﴾ أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ الذي فعل هذا بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى ﴿Is not He who did this able to give life to the dead?﴾

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: al-Qati'i related to us, who said: al-Kindi related to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Bannan al-Saffar related to us, who said: Shu'bah related to us, who said: Yunus al-Tawil, companion of Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, related to me, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: When this verse was revealed, أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Glory be to You, and yes." [76]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Rabi'i related to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ayyub al-Makhzumi related to us, who said: Salih ibn Malik related to us, who said: Abu Nawfal 'Ali ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever recites سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلى, whether he is an imam or otherwise, let him say: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.' And whoever recites لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ, and when he reaches its end, let him say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and yes,' whether he is an imam or otherwise."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 75, verses 29–40:**

وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ "And the shin is wound around the shin" (﴿And one leg is entwined with another﴾). Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "The world is joined to the Hereafter." This is also the report of Abu al-Jawza' and 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas, and the report of 'Awf and Mansur from al-Hasan. Al-Wali and Badhan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The affair of this world is joined to the affair of the Hereafter, so it is the last day of the days of this world and the first day of the days of the Hereafter." This is the report of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid. Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid said: "The deeds of this world are joined to the deeds of the Hereafter." Al-Dahhak said: "The people prepare his body and the angels prepare his soul." Sufyan narrated from a man, from al-Hasan, from Mujahid, the two of them saying: "Life and death are gathered in him." Qatadah said: "Hardship upon hardship." Bishr ibn al-Muhajir reported from al-Hasan who said: "They are your two shins when they are wrapped in the shroud," and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab held this view.

We were informed by 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid, who said: Abu Muhammad al-Muzani informed us, who said: Mutayyin related to us, who said: Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, who said: Khalid ibn Qays related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: "His legs died and did not carry him, and they were upon him as a burden." Shu'bah reported from Qatadah who said: "An affair that comes to him when one leg strikes the other." Abu Malik: "He puts them on at death." 'Ikrimah: "Departure from the world to the Hereafter." Abu Yahya from Mujahid: "Affliction upon affliction."

Al-Qurtubi: "The affair upon the affair." Zayd ibn Aslam: "The shroud's shin joined to the corpse's shin." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Calamities followed one upon another upon him." Al-Suddi: "He does not emerge from one distress except that a greater one comes to him." The Arabs mention the shin only in trials and hardships, and from their well-known proverb: "He does not loose the shin except while holding a shin." Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

"I have been kept awake by a worry that visits me, and the soul is full of scruples and anxieties,
Seeking refuge in the gravel when the night of completeness kept me awake, which I endure on a shin."

That is: upon weariness and hardship.

Ibn 'Ata' said: "There gathers upon him the hardship of departing the homeland of the world, family and children, and the hardship of coming before his Lord, not knowing what he will be presented with." For this reason 'Uthman ibn 'Affan said: "I have never seen a scene except that the grave is more frightful than it, because it is the last of the abodes of this world and the first of the abodes of the Hereafter." Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "When the deceased enters the grave, four angels stand at the edge of his grave: one at his head, a second at his feet, a third on his right, and a fourth on his left. The one at his head says: 'O son of Adam, the terms have ended and the hopes have been cut off.' The one on his right says: 'Wealth has gone and deeds remain.' The one on his left says: 'Preoccupations have gone and calamity remains.' The one at his feet says: 'Blessed are you for your earnings, if your earnings were lawful and you were occupied in serving the Lord of Majesty.'"

إِلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَساقُ ﴿To your Lord, that Day, is the driving﴾: the final end and the return. The angels drive his soul to where Allah, the Exalted, has commanded them.
